name: application-approval-request-card
title: Approval Request Card
description: Access/approval request card with requester, resource, an optional note, and Approve/Reject actions that resolve to a real decided state.
useWhen: Building an admin queue where a reviewer approves or rejects pending requests one at a time.
Each request benefits from requester identity, the specific resource being requested, and optional free-text justification.
You want the card to visually resolve (badge change, actions disappearing) once a decision is made, rather than staying interactive after resolution.
avoidWhen: Requests need bulk approve/reject across many rows at once — a `tables` row with checkboxes and a `bulk-action-bar` fits that better.
There's no reviewable request, just a status to display — a plain `badges` pill is sufficient without the action buttons.
The decision needs additional required input (e.g. a reason for rejection) — extend this pattern with a confirmation step rather than a single click.
responsiveBehavior: Single-column card; the requester row and note stack naturally at any width, with actions right-aligned in the footer.
accessibility: The status badge text ("Pending", "Approved", "Rejected") is the source of truth, not just badge color, satisfying colorblind and screen-reader users alike.
Approve/Reject are separate, clearly labeled buttons rather than a single ambiguous toggle.
Once resolved, the action buttons are removed rather than disabled-but-visible, preventing a false impression that the decision can still be changed from this view.
The requester avatar is decorative (empty alt) since the name is present as adjacent text.
